newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Acacia shares dip on Helix buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Acacia shares dip on Helix buy.

text.p: The shares of gold miner Acacia Resources Ltd drifted lower on Friday after the company announced that it had bought a 17.4 percent stake in Gawler Craton gold explorer Helix Resources NL for A$38 million.
At 11.05 p.m. (0005 GMT), Acacia shares were 12 cents weaker at A$2.27 on turnover of 1.8 million shares. Helix shares were 12 cents higher at A$4.82.

"The perception amongst some investors is that Acacia has payed top dollar for Helix and this has created some uncertainty about the outlook for the company," said Martin Angel, a dealer at Perth broker, Eyres Reed.
Diamond producer Ashton Mining Ltd said on Thursday it had sold its holding of 5.97 million Helix ordinary shares, representing about 12.89 percent.
Brokers said the shares were sold at A$4.45 each, well below the Thursday closing price of A$4.70.
Angel said the jury was still out as to whether Acacia had paid to much for its Helix stake.
"To justify it (the purchase) we need to see some more encouraging results from Helix and this is what the market is waiting for," Angel said.
Another factor which may be depressing Acacia stock was investors' fear that Acacia may launch a takeover offer for Helix sometime in the future, Angel said.
This factor was being reflected in the price of Helix stock which hit a life high of A$4.98 in mid-morning trade.
